content_of_post_to_comment: GIFTEDNESS IS A FORM OF NEURODIVERGENCE People know that autism, ADHD, dyslexia, dyscalculia, intellectual disability, and other learning disorders & mental health conditions are neurodivergent. But they often don’t realize or they forget that giftedness is also a form of neurodivergence. Gifted cognition is found in only around 5% of the general population, so it is in the literal sense neuro-divergent from the roughly 95% norm (as far as high intellectual complexity goes). People often forget about giftedness being a neurodivergence, or don’t realize it to begin with, because they think of neurodivergence as being connected to unusual needs, often with a disability label attached, and they assume gifted people are just better at the usual things than average (or they don’t believe giftedness exists to begin with!). But giftedness does exist and gifted people do also have very unique and challenging needs due to their high intellectual complexity. Without proper support, giftedness can at times feel like a burden for gifted people. We like to raise awareness about giftedness as a neurodivergence, so that health professionals and mental health professionals, managers and bosses, teachers and educators, parents and other carers, partners and friends, and researchers and policy makers will recognize and provide support for gifted people’s unique needs, starting from the earliest of age and well into adulthood.
